org-wide [from, to, kind, staff, sentiment, ...] | client_checkins: Every client check-in / feedback record org-wide [from, to, client_ref, staff, outcome, ...] | google_reviews: The business's Google handbook did not answer [status] | training_modules: Training modules [status, module_id] | training_assignments: Who is assigned which training module, with status and deadline [module_id] | company_documents: SOP files the business uploaded, with the Flows and recurring tasks Sergio suggested... | findings: Product gaps / bugs filed on the /development board | financial_reports: Org-wide money rollups [from, to] | lead_pursuits: The Leads ledger [from, to, active, owed_by, task_status, ...] | campaigns: The Growth campaigns list [status, campaign] | campaign_recipients: Who each campaign reached [campaign, state, client_ref, from, to, ...] | flows: The business's flows as the Automations page lists them [flow, active] | scanners: The business's Scanners as the Scanners page lists them [scanner, enabled] | import_jobs: Imports as the Imports page and Data sources list them [status, source] | conversation_flows: Each time a flow or program [flow, status, outcome, client_ref, from, ...] | settings: Every setting of this business, from the one settings registry [area]. read('catalog') gives each entity's full description, every filter and field, and which this caller may read. E.g. read("bookings",{status:"cancelled"}), read("conversation_transcript",{client_ref:"Maria Lopez"}), read("cockpit_queue"), read("settings",{area:"ai"}) to learn which model powers you and where to switch it. A client_ref is a FULL name or an id (a bare first name may need disambiguation. Answer a needs_disambiguation result by re-reading with the candidate's id). from/to dates are the business's local calendar days. A value-set filter (each entity's setFilters in read('catalog'): status, state, outcome…) takes one value, a list (["completed","scheduled"] or "completed,scheduled"), a negation ("!cancelled"), or exclude_<key> (e.g. exclude_status:"cancelled"); an unknown value is an error naming the valid ones. A ref filter (each entity's refFilters in read('catalog'): client_ref, staff) takes one ref, a JSON array of refs (matches any; a single string is always ONE ref, commas included), "!ref" or exclude_<key> to drop, up to 25 refs per read; a ref in the set that matches no one or several people returns that ref's no_match / needs_disambiguation. SEVERAL AT ONCE: conversations (conversation_id or client_ref, up to 10); conversation_transcript (conversation_id or client_ref, up to 10); client_case_file (conversation_id or client_ref, up to 5); staff_detail (staff, up to 10) take a list of values and answer every one in ONE call (items[] in the order asked); never loop one read per person. Everything is org-scoped and read-only; you never pass an organization id. List reads carry returned/total/truncated: when truncated is true you saw only the most recent `returned` of `total` (or of more). Say so plainly and narrow with filters (a date range from/to, a status, a client). TO RETRIEVE A SET COMPLETELY: if truncated, page with options.limit = N (up to 100) and options.offset = 0, N, 2N … until returned < N or offset >= total. Pages are stable (ties break on id), so paging never repeats or skips a row. A group_by read pages its GROUPS the same way: groups_total says how many exist and next_offset (with paging_hint) is the options.offset of the next page. TO COUNT ("how many X", "bookings per status"): read with the filter and use `total`. Issue one filtered read per value and read each `total`; NEVER eyeball or tally a capped page of rows.

limit.description: Max rows (default ~25, capped per entity, never above 100).

list_limit.description: Rows per nested list by its key, e.g. {"clientRelationships": 10} (up to 100).

list_offset.description: Page a nested list by its key, e.g. {"clientRelationships": 25}. Every list in a payload states its own count in list_disclosure[key] (returned, total, truncated, next_offset); disclosed_list names the list the top-level returned/total describe.

max_bytes.description: A search (communications, conversation_transcript, calls with search) returns the hit count plus the newest hits that fit 20480 bytes (default 20 hits) and next_offset; raise this (up to 204800) for bigger pages.
